items.detail: Types, declarations, statements and expressions as tagged nodes; the JSON Schema is generated from the model and drift-checked.
items.label: cir/1, defined once in Rust

items.detail: An unknown field, an unknown kind, an expression without a type and any format other than cir/1 are refused.
items.label: Strict reading

items.detail: One byte sequence per document; codespec validate --canonical refuses any other.
items.label: Canonical encoding

items.detail: codespec-read-go lifts one Go package; reading twice gives the same bytes, equal to the checked-in document of every example.
items.label: Go reader on go/types

items.detail: A construct cir/1 cannot express (a goroutine) is kept verbatim as a foreign statement and listed as a refusal; the Rust writer then refuses the function holding it.
items.label: Foreign statements and refusals

items.detail: codespec-read-rust: Rust to cir/1 with its own name and type resolution for the cir/1 subset, so Rust to cir/1 to Go runs under the harness. Decided for 0.1.0, in progress; not in this tree yet.
items.label: Rust reader on syn

items.detail: A comma-ok map lookup followed by an early-return guard becomes one lookup_else statement.
items.label: lookup-guard

items.detail: shared, messages, fallible, comma_ok, read_only, displays and unordered_iteration, computed once per module for every writer.
items.label: Seven facts

items.detail: codespec pass over its own output gives the same bytes.
items.label: Passes reach their fixed point in one run

items.detail: codespec-write-go writes gofmt-clean, vetted Go; the reader reads it back to the same cir/1.
items.label: Go writer on go/ast and go/printer

items.detail: codespec-write-rust writes a Cargo crate from the module and its facts; the crate builds without warnings.
items.label: Rust writer on syn and prettyplease

items.detail: A module without facts is refused whole by the Rust writer, naming the pass to run.
items.label: Writers decide nothing the facts do not say

items.detail: The original Go, the Go output and the Rust output of orders agree on 200 traces of 300 commands.

items.detail: A one-token change in the Rust output exits 1 naming the seed, the implementation and the first differing line.
items.label: A planted change is caught

items.detail: SplitMix64 and integer arithmetic only: one seed gives the same trace bytes everywhere.
items.label: Traces pinned across platforms
